rationale: Defines 'prescribed' as fixed by rules under the Act, but a definitions list that does not state the application fee the RTI Rules, 2012 set.
Provides for appeals against a refusal or delay and does not state the fee payable with an application.
Requires an application to be accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed, but does not state the amount fixed by the RTI Rules, 2012.

target: Right to Information Rules, 2012, application fee
rationale: The fee payable with an application is prescribed by the RTI Rules, 2012, which are not admitted text.
Bars a civil court from entertaining a suit about a direction under the Act, but does not provide the appeal to the National Green Tribunal.
Provides appeals under the RTI Act to a senior officer and the Information Commission, not an appeal to the National Green Tribunal.
Allows an appeal to the National Commission against certain consumer-authority orders, which is a different Act and a different forum.
Gives authorised officers powers of entry and inspection and does not create an appeal against a direction.
Lets a person aggrieved by a direction under section 5 appeal to the National Green Tribunal in accordance with the National Green Tribunal Act.
Confers the power to issue the closure and regulation directions against which the appeal lies, but does not itself provide the appeal.

target: National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, appeal against a direction under the Environment (Protection) Act
rationale: Section 5A sends the appeal to the National Green Tribunal in accordance with that Act, which is not admitted.
Defines misrepresentation in the Contract Act and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Sets the Information Commissions' complaint powers and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Requires intimation of foreign contribution received and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Protects action taken in good faith under environmental law and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Requires measures for adult education of persons with disabilities and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Lists the Central Consumer Protection Authority's functions and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Deals with assignment of copyright and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Requires accounts and audit of legal-services authorities and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Provides an appeal from an Internal Committee recommendation and is not section 18 of the Real Estate Act.
Makes the promoter liable to return the amount with interest, or to pay interest for delay, and to compensate the allottee for defective title or other breaches.
Appoints an adjudicating officer to award compensation under section 18, which is the procedure the compensation right depends on.
Sets the promoter's duties after a project is registered and does not say whether or how a real estate agent must register.
Forbids a real estate agent to facilitate a sale in a registered project without registration and sets the application, grant, deemed registration, number and revocation.
Imposes a daily penalty on a real estate agent who contravenes the registration requirement in section 9, which is the penalty rather than the registration rule.
Lets the government call for information and inspect records and does not set the Internal Committee's inquiry time or procedure.
Requires the Internal Committee to inquire according to service rules or the prescribed manner, with a hearing where both parties are employees, and to finish within ninety days.
Allows conciliation before the inquiry begins and, if a settlement is reached, bars any further inquiry.
Lets the committee, during the inquiry, recommend transfer, leave or other interim relief, which is a step in the inquiry rather than its time limit.
Requires the inquiry findings to be reported within ten days of completion and acted on within sixty days, which follows the inquiry rather than fixing its length.
Lets the Authority recall unsafe goods and stop unfair practices after a hearing, but does not set the directions or penalties for a false or misleading advertisement.
Protects officers for acts done in good faith and does not confer any power over advertisements.
Lets the Authority order a false or misleading advertisement to be discontinued or modified and impose penalties, including a ban on the endorser.
Charges the Authority with ensuring that no false or misleading advertisement is made, but the concrete orders and penalties are in section 21.
Lets the Authority hold a preliminary inquiry and cause an investigation into a false or misleading advertisement, which is the step before the order.
Sets how a Permanent Lok Adalat conducts proceedings and does not list the functions of the National Legal Services Authority.
Provides for authentication of electronic records by digital signature and has nothing to do with the National Legal Services Authority.
Authorises rules under the food-security law and does not state the functions of the National Legal Services Authority.
Authorises rules on seafarer certificates and does not state the functions of the National Legal Services Authority.
Lets the Central Authority make regulations, which is a regulation-making power rather than the list of the Authority's functions.
Requires the Central Authority to establish and apply the National Legal Aid Fund, which is one duty and not the functions section.
The section listing the functions of the Central Authority, which is the National Legal Services Authority, is not admitted.
Admits an out-of-school child to an age-appropriate class with special training, which is a different admission rule and not the 25% entry-level quota.
Requires recognised institutions to admit children with disabilities without discrimination, which is a similar admission duty in a different Act and not the 25% quota.
Reserves at least five per cent of seats in government and aided higher-education institutions for persons with benchmark disabilities, a different reservation in the wrong Act.
Requires specified schools to admit children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups to at least twenty-five per cent of the strength of class I, and to give them free education.
Section 12 applies the 25% duty by cross-reference to the definitions of the school categories, weaker section and disadvantaged group, which are not admitted.
